title: Vendi Anomaly Scores for Efficient and Accurate Anomaly Detection
why_read: An interesting reframing of anomaly detection around dataset diversity rather than density, with strong benchmark results.
analysis: Most anomaly detection methods flag outliers by looking at local density, distance from a fitted distribution, or isolation-based heuristics, all of which require tuning choices like neighborhood size. This paper instead measures how much removing a given data point changes the overall diversity of the dataset, using a metric called the Vendi score borrowed from ecology and quantum statistics. The method needs no hyperparameter tuning and scales linearly with dataset size, and the authors report state-of-the-art results across 148 benchmark datasets. This is a genuinely different angle on a well-studied problem, worth a look for ML practitioners working on outlier or novelty detection.
